## Trial `repair-application-permissions-c__xiguxmW`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly repaired /srv/inventory ownership (inventorysvc:inventory-readers) and permissions (750/640), verified group-read and other-deny behavior with disposable test accounts, and proved data preservation via matching sha256 checksums before and after the change. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: healthy pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, unreachability during the transition, a changed boot_id, and full recovery of ownership, permissions, and data integrity post-restart, consistent with the fixed global boot-identity snapshots.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.950 | 12/4 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **ownership — Satisfied:** Existing data under /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
  - **Why:** inventorysvc system user and inventory-readers group were created (cmd-505a25ac08f44462), then /srv/inventory recursively chowned to inventorysvc:inventory-readers with ls -l confirming ownership on all directories and files (cmd-5cb7a267aee443a0), and re-confirmed after restart (cmd-ea1a335c310e404d).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-505a25ac08f44462`, `cmd-5cb7a267aee443a0`, `cmd-ea1a335c310e404d`
- **group-readable — Satisfied:** Data readable by inventory-readers group
  - **Why:** Permissions set to u=rwX,g=rX,o= (750/640) via chmod -R (cmd-5cb7a267aee443a0). A test user added to inventory-readers successfully read records.csv (READER_OK), confirming group read access works (cmd-9c86e5b78f6e45bb).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-5cb7a267aee443a0`, `cmd-9c86e5b78f6e45bb`
- **other-inaccessible — Satisfied:** Data inaccessible to other (non-owner, non-group) users
  - **Why:** An unrelated test user (outsideruser, no inventory-readers membership) was denied at both file read (Permission denied, exit 1) and directory listing (Permission denied, exit 2), directly demonstrating 'other' access is blocked (cmd-9c86e5b78f6e45bb).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9c86e5b78f6e45bb`
- **content-preserved — Satisfied:** Preserve existing contents of /srv/inventory during repair
  - **Why:** sha256 checksums and raw content of records.csv/config.json were captured before the chown/chmod (cmd-f000b66f37854e5c) and match the prepared baseline exactly (records.csv=bad65b86..., config.json=1448a747...). After the permission change, checksums were re-verified identical (cmd-a5b32e3d5d734ebb), and again after the node restart (cmd-ea1a335c310e404d), confirming no data mutation occurred at any point.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f000b66f37854e5c`, `cmd-a5b32e3d5d734ebb`, `cmd-ea1a335c310e404d`
- **restart-recovery — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of task contract)
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id (8f258838-...) and a healthy baseline (permissions, ownership, checksums) were captured (cmd-049febc443984d6a), matching the global before/after-prepare boot-identity snapshot. systemctl reboot was issued with an acknowledgement returned before disconnect (cmd-c34821befda94c0f). The node was unreachable during the transition (cmd-48a11645aedb444e, cmd-3fd8b631afbb4226) and then returned a different boot_id (6714a474-..., cmd-b081046e2bc4458d), matching the global after-executor snapshot. Post-restart, ownership, group, permissions, and byte-identical checksums were all reverified (cmd-ea1a335c310e404d), and global snapshots show no failed services or package-health regressions after restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-049febc443984d6a`, `cmd-c34821befda94c0f`, `cmd-48a11645aedb444e`, `cmd-3fd8b631afbb4226`, `cmd-b081046e2bc4458d`, `cmd-ea1a335c310e404d`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. Two temporary test users (testreader, outsideruser) were created solely to validate group/other access boundaries (cmd-9c86e5b78f6e45bb), a reasonable, bounded verification step directly supporting the readability/inaccessibility requirements. Their removal initially failed because processes from the sudo -u invocations were still attached (cmd-989a9ad59e9c4092), requiring a follow-up pkill + userdel (cmd-25488903bfb44e7b); final id checks confirm both users were fully removed. This is a minor, self-corrected cleanup wrinkle rather than residue left behind - global after_executor listening-sockets/failed-services/package-health snapshots show no test-user artifacts or degraded state post-restart. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were observed; all state changes (group/user creation, chown, chmod, temporary test accounts, reboot) map directly to the task or the restart-evidence protocol.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-9c86e5b78f6e45bb`, `cmd-989a9ad59e9c4092`, `cmd-25488903bfb44e7b`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`
